co_sweat_loaf_aka_big_dogs.blurb: A quartz monzonite dome in the South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon west of Lyons, reached by a short creek crossing from a roadside pullout. Most of the 17 climbs are trad, built around crack systems, with some faces bolted to join them up; a few boulder problems sit alongside. Many lines run two or three pitches, though anchors partway up let you do a shorter outing. Difficulty is concentrated at 5.9 to 5.11, with a handful of 5.12s and a few problems from VB to V8. The main face looks west-northwest and catches plenty of afternoon sun, so it suits cooler days. Only a portion of the dome's potential has been climbed.

co_wild_rock.blurb: A steep sport crag tucked into the trees just off the road on Independence Pass, east of Aspen, at around 10,400 feet. Of its 17 climbs, most are bolted, with a couple of trad lines and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.7 and 5.8 but the weight sits in the 5.13s, making it a destination for strong sport climbers rather than beginners, with only a few warm-ups. The harder lines face east, getting sun early and shade later in the day. Reaching the base means a short path through woods and then a talus slog. Boulders scattered nearby add bouldering options.

co_rock_pile_the.blurb: A granite crag above Buena Vista, at roughly 9,300 feet. It is a friendly place to learn trad: most of the 17 climbs are gear routes, with a few sport lines, and the grades run mainly from 5.6 to 5.8 with some 5.9 to 5.11 above that. Many routes finish at fixed anchors, so you can top-rope or practise placing gear in safety. The walk-in crosses a field and climbs a series of ramps. The wall is very sunny with little shade apart from some trees, so carry water. It tends to be uncrowded.
co_rock_pile_the.approach: Walk across a field from the parking area, then up a series of ramps to the base of the crag, around 15 to 20 minutes.

co_sapper_cave_the.blurb: A quiet, wooded cave in Rifle Mountain Park, a short way up canyon from the Project Wall. All 17 climbs are bolted limestone sport routes on steep, overhanging stone, with outlying lines on the walls either side of the cave. Grades are hard: a few 5.11s, most at 5.12, and several 5.13s, so it is not a place for beginners. It stays shaded until early afternoon in summer, making it a good morning stop. A climbers' trail leads in from the road, and the most popular lines can mean a wait on busy weekends.
